identity.title: ALMA Observations of Elias 2-24: A Protoplanetary Disk with Multiple Gaps in the Ophiuchus Molecular Cloud

findings_qualitative.value: Third gap at 0.18'' identified in the uvmem image; it survives noise realizations

evidence.quote: This third gap survives the different realization of noise injected to the visibilities and it is seen as a change in slope in the deprojected radial average.

claims.experiment: 1.3 mm imaging with clean and uvmem
claims.finding: Disk has three partially resolved gaps

evidence.quote: report the presence of three partially resolved concentric gaps located at $\sim$20, 52, and 87 au from the star.

claims.experiment: RT model midplane temperature at gap locations
claims.finding: Temperatures close to CO and N2 condensation fronts

evidence.quote: very close to the expected snow-lines of CO (23-28 K) and N$_{2}$ (12-15 K).

claims.hypothesis: Forming planets can carve the gaps
claims.experiment: Hill radius argument and missing mass from surface density
claims.result: Planet masses 0.02-8 MJup versus missing mass 4-20 MJup
claims.finding: Enough mass to form such planets

evidence.quote: the amount of “missing mass" at the location of each one of these gaps (between 4 and 20 $M_{\mathrm{Jup}}$) is more than sufficient to account for the formation of such planets.

why_this_data.value: Disk size, brightness and orientation allow substructure search at modest resolution

evidence.quote: The size, brightness, and orientation of its disk, allow us to search for substructure in Elias  2-24 using what now can be considered modest resolution.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Water, ammonia and clathrate snow-lines lie at <20 au and are unresolved

evidence.quote: all these temperatures correspond to stellocentric distances $<$ 20 au, which are not resolved by our observations.

limitations_admitted.value: Gaps only partially resolved, degeneracy between width and depth

evidence.quote: Since the gaps are only partially resolved, there is a degeneracy between the width and the depth of the gaps.
However, other potential explanations still exist, including magneto-hydrodynamic effects and disk instabilities.

referee_caveats_inferred: Smooth disk model fitted without gaps while temperatures taken at gap locations
Snow-line match relies on a broad temperature range and a single midplane model
Planet masses depend on the assumed 4-8 Hill radii and the gap widths from partially resolved data
Very short 45 s integration; uvmem super-resolution may bias gap depths
